status: Reviewed territorial subsidies of the representative models (owner decisions 67-70, 74 and 76-78, 2026-11-24).
rule: Territorial models show each level's cost before subsidies (the published tariff: subsidy prices are stored as conditional alternatives or conditional credits and stay out of it) and, where 'jurisdictions' allows it, the cost after the automatic subsidies below (treatments reference_rates, first_block_price and per_kwh_credit) and the 'subsidy' entries of data/models/percentage_riders.json. A subsidy counts as automatic only where an official source says so (decision 67): an applied program quotes that text in 'automatic'. Reference rates replace the whole tariff of the zone records they apply to ('applies_to'), every charge and rider (decision 78); a first-block price replaces the whole per-kWh price of the first-block kWh in the tariff in force, riders and credits included (decisions 76 and 78); a per-kWh credit with within_first_block false applies to the kWh above the first block. Programs with treatment 'disclose' are named, never applied. A subsidy whose price is not stored for a zone record is not applied there and is named (with its reviewed 'absent' reason when one is given), so the after-subsidy cost never claims a subsidy that the sources do not establish; a zone record that a reference-rate program applies to but whose reference rates are missing is not computable after subsidies. Seasonal first blocks are priced once per season and month-weighted (decision 68; usage_levels.json seasons). After-subsidy figures are published before tax only (decision 74).
tax_note: After-subsidy costs are shown before tax only, until bills or official text confirm the GST base on subsidised bills (owner decision 74, 2026-11-24). The with-tax figures are computed on the cost before subsidies, as for the provinces.

commercial.reason: No automatic subsidy for general service: the Yukon Affordability Rate Relief is for the 'Residential - Non Government customer class only. Not applicable to any commercial, industrial or government customers.' (Affordability Rate Relief Rebate, effective 2026 10 01). The commercial models show the cost before subsidies only.

No after-subsidy cost is computed for general service. The GNWT Cost of Living Subsidy also applies automatically to commercial customers (NTPC, February 2026 Rider Explanation: 'This credit automatically applies to all eligible residential and commercial customers, including local governments (Hamlets, Towns, Bands).'), but NTPC publishes no credit value for general service: none is printed in its rate schedule effective June 1, 2026 (https://www.ntpc.com/sites/default/files/2026-06/NTPC%20Rate%20Schedule%20-%20June%201%202026.pdf), on its residential rates page or on its business-service pages (read 2026-11-24), and the stored general service records carry none. TPSP is for residential customers only. Naka's GREP general-service reference rates apply only in its Thermal zone, whose general service is not stored.

residential.reason: Qulliq Energy does not publish the price paid on the Nunavut Electricity Subsidy Program allowance (700 kWh per 30-day period from April to September, 1,000 kWh from October to March, for one residence), so the Nunavut models show the cost before subsidy only and no price is invented (owner decision 69, 2026-11-24).

commercial.reason: No automatic subsidy for general service: the Nunavut Electricity Subsidy Program is for non-government residential customers (Qulliq Energy, Customer Rates page, 'Non-Government Residential (Domestic) Customers'). The commercial models show the cost before subsidies only.

programs.name: GNWT Territorial Power Support Program (TPSP)
programs.component_name_regex: ^GNWT TPSP Subsidised First-Block Energy Price \((September 1 to March 31|April 1 to August 31)\)$

replaces.text: the whole per-kWh price of the first-block kWh: the energy charge, NTPC's per-kWh riders and the GNWT Cost of Living Subsidy (the first-block price is all-in, owner decision 76); the monthly service charge stays, and the riders and the credit apply to the kWh above the block

absent.reason: NTPC's published 'Your cost' price and stated saving for the Snare zone (Behchokǫ̀, Dettah) do not reconcile, so no first-block price is stored; TPSP is omitted there and disclosed (owner decision 77, 2026-11-24)

automatic.quote: Residential customers are automatically enrolled in the Territorial Power Support Program when they set up their household account. Customers can only have one TPSP account at any given time.

programs.quote: Their TPSP program ensures that all NWT households can, with modest energy saving efforts, pay the same low power rate as Yellowknife. From September 1 to March 31 each year, residential customers only pay the Yellowknife rate on the first 1,000 kilowatt hours (kWh) of power that they consume. After 1,000 kWh, each additional kilowatt hour is charged at the Zone Rate.
programs.location: Territorial Power Support Program (TPSP) page (read 2026-11-24); first-block prices: Residential Electrical Rates, effective September 1, 2026 (https://www.ntpc.com/customer-service/residential-service/residential-electrical-rates), 'Your cost' column
programs.evidence: Residential Electrical Rates, effective September 1, 2026: under 'Up to 1000 kWh' the 'Your cost' column lists only 'Energy charge 36.50 cents / kWh', and the riders and the GNWT Cost of Living Subsidy are listed only under 'Each additional kWh' (Thermal: 84.68 = 88.96 + 1.01 + 7.72 + 0.42 - 13.43 cents). The page's saving statements are consistent with an all-in block: 'If you use 1000 kWh, you save $524.60 per month -- that's the amount paid by the GNWT Territorial Power Support Program.' ($524.60 = 1,000 kWh x (88.96 - 36.50) cents in the Thermal zone; Norman Wells $348.00 = 1,000 x (71.30 - 36.50) cents): they equal the energy-charge difference because no rider is listed on the first-block kWh in either column ('Your cost' and 'Actual cost'). Naka's July 2026 rate-update notice shows the same program's first block all-in.
programs.note: The first-block price is all-in (owner decision 76, 2026-11-24): the first-block kWh pay 36.50 cents in place of the energy charge, NTPC's per-kWh riders and the Cost of Living credit; the monthly service charge stays. TPSP is omitted and disclosed in the Snare zone (owner decision 77); NTPC publishes no TPSP price for Fort Resolution, Fort Smith and Hay River, whose after-subsidy cost has the Cost of Living credit on every kWh.

programs.name: GNWT Territorial Power Support Program (TPSP)
programs.component_name_regex: ^GNWT TPSP First-Block Energy Price \((September 1 to March 31|April 1 to August 31)\)$

replaces.text: the whole per-kWh price of the first-block kWh in the tariff in force (all-in, owner decisions 76 and 78): in the Thermal zone the GREP reference energy price; elsewhere Naka's supply and fuel charges, Riders A and F and the percentage riders' share; the customer charge (in the Thermal zone the GREP reference customer charge) and its riders stay

absent.reason: the rate schedule makes TPSP available throughout Naka's service territory excluding the Snare Zone (Yellowknife)

automatic.quote: Applicable to all non-government Residential Service customers
automatic.location: Rate Schedule effective July 1, 2026, Territorial Power Subsidy Program (TPSP), PDF page 32
automatic.note: Owner decision 67 (2026-11-24): the NWT TPSP is automatic; NTPC: 'Residential customers are automatically enrolled in the Territorial Power Support Program when they set up their household account.'

programs.quote: The Territorial Support is limited to 1000 kW.h per month during September to March and 600 kW.h per month during April to August, pro-rated on a 30 day charge period basis. The Territorial Support Rate is based on the Snare Zone (Yellowknife) reference rate of 36.50¢/ kW.h.
programs.location: Rate Schedule effective July 1, 2026, Territorial Power Subsidy Program (TPSP), PDF page 32
programs.evidence: Naka Power, Electricity Rate Updates - Effective July 1, 2026 (https://www.nakapower.com/en-ca/customer-billing-rates/rates-regulations/rate-updates-july-2026.html), typical non-government residential customer using 600 kWh ('Residential includes GREP (Thermal Zone only) and TPSP'): Taltson +$10.00 = 600 kWh x (36.50 - 35.23) cents (the Yellowknife reference rate before and after July 1) + $18.00 x (54.9% - 41.7%) (the percentage riders on the customer charge). The first-block kWh pay the reference rate in place of the zone's whole energy price, and the reference rate is itself Yellowknife's whole energy price (23.72 cents x 1.08199 + 10.84 cents = 36.50 cents).
programs.note: Available throughout Naka's service territory excluding the Snare Zone (Yellowknife), whose records carry no first-block price. In the Thermal zone the first block applies on top of the GREP reference rates (owner decision 78): the notice's typical Thermal non-government bill changes by +$7.62 = 600 kWh x (36.50 - 35.23) cents. The block is applied per average month as decided (1,000 or 600 kWh); the pro-rating on a 30-day charge period is not modelled.

programs.name: GNWT Cost of Living Subsidy

automatic.quote: This credit automatically applies to all eligible residential and commercial customers, including local governments (Hamlets, Towns, Bands).
automatic.location: February 2026 Rider Explanation, GNWT Cost of Living Subsidy ('Exceptions: It does not apply to Federal or GNWT accounts, nor does it apply to Local Housing Corporations.')

programs.quote: If you use more than 1000 kWh per month between September 1 and March 31 you will pay 84.68 cents per kWh.
programs.location: Residential Electrical Rates, effective September 1, 2026: the credit is listed under 'Each additional kWh' (Thermal -13.43, Norman Wells -12.35 cents/kWh) and for every kWh in Fort Resolution, Fort Smith (-13.18) and Hay River (-13.53)
programs.note: Applied to the kWh above the TPSP first block, whose price is all-in (owner decision 76, 2026-11-24: the residential page lists the credit only under 'Each additional kWh'; 84.68 = 88.96 + 1.01 + 7.72 + 0.42 - 13.43 cents), and to every kWh where no first block applies (Fort Resolution, Fort Smith and Hay River). Approved until March 2028 (NTPC).

programs.name: GNWT Rate Equalization Program (GREP)

replaces.text: Naka's own Thermal tariff, every charge and rider (the customer, supply and fuel charges, Rider A and the percentage Riders R and E), by the GREP reference customer charge and reference energy price; the TPSP first block then replaces the reference energy price on the first-block kWh

automatic.quote: Applicable • To non-government residential and general service customers in the Thermal Rate Zone.
automatic.location: Rate Schedule, GNWT Rate Equalization Program (GREP) (effective June 1, 2026), PDF page 33
automatic.note: Owner decision 78 (2026-11-24): GREP is applied for non-government Thermal residential customers. Naka's Electricity Rate Updates - Effective July 1, 2026 (https://www.nakapower.com/en-ca/customer-billing-rates/rates-regulations/rate-updates-july-2026.html), note 2 to its rate-impact table: 'For Non-Government Customers: Residential includes GREP (Thermal Zone only) and TPSP'.

programs.quote: The GREP reference rates are based on the sum of rates and riders for Non-Government customers in NTPC’s Thermal Zone which are shown in the following Table. Component Residential General Service Customer / Demand $18.00 / month $8.00 / kW / month Energy 83.94 ¢ / kWh 72.01 ¢ / kWh
programs.location: Rate Schedule, GNWT Rate Equalization Program (GREP) (effective June 1, 2026), PDF page 33
programs.evidence: Naka's July 1, 2026 rate-update notice: a typical Thermal non-government residential customer using 600 kWh changes by +$7.62 (+3.3%) = 600 kWh x (36.50 - 35.23) cents, the change of the TPSP Yellowknife reference rate alone, while Naka's own Thermal riders changed on July 1 (the government customer, who pays them, changes by +$99.26). This reconciles only when the non-government bill is the GREP reference customer charge with the TPSP first block ($18.00 + 600 kWh x 36.50 cents).
programs.note: The reference rates are all-in ('the sum of rates and riders'), so in the after-subsidy cost they replace Naka's own Thermal charges and every rider instead of adding to them; the cost before subsidies stays Naka's own Thermal tariff. Applied in the Thermal zone only; Naka's Thermal general service is not stored, so no commercial model uses GREP.

programs.name: Nunavut Electricity Subsidy Program (NESP)
programs.quote: These customers are entitled to receive a subsidy of 700 kWh for each 30-day period from April 1 to September 30 and 1000 kWh for each 30-day period from October 1 to March 31. Any consumption that exceeds the subsidy threshold is billed at a Residential Non-Government rate at full cost.
programs.location: Customer Rates page, Non-Government Residential (Domestic) Customers (read 2026-11-24)
programs.reason: Qulliq Energy does not publish the price paid on the subsidised allowance (700 kWh per 30-day period from April to September, 1,000 kWh from October to March, one residence), so the allowance is stored without a price and the Nunavut models are before subsidy only (owner decision 69). QEC also states that the interim service-charge increase from $18 to $36 a month 'will be fully covered by the Nunavut Electricity Subsidy Program (NESP), and customers will not be billed for this charge'; the cost before subsidy includes the full $36.
